variables.className: Official class name and its recognizable identity
variables.identityNotes: Observed species, face, hairstyle, mask/headwear, original palette and costume from the actual game model
variables.individualPose: A new expression, pose and small class-related story specific to this one character
variables.watercolorWash: A restrained desaturated color that supports the class palette
variables.headSlot: One-based face/hairstyle position from game-looks.json; do not confuse with internal labels
variables.headSkin: Exact source texture id for the selected game face/hairstyle
variables.bodySkin: Exact source texture id for the default outfit; alternate outfits come after heads

referenceImagesInOrder: The approved male Iop portrait: use its ink-and-watercolor treatment only, never its anatomy, colors, identity or pose
A close front/three-quarter render of the target class and gender from the Dofus game client
A second angle of that exact target game model

referencePreparation.source: Dofus client assets extracted with scripts/extract-characters.py
referencePreparation.identityMapping: docs/brand/profile-avatars/game-looks.json: class, sex, one-based head slot, source head/body ids, skins and original colors
referencePreparation.framing: Render a close view of the head and upper torso at sufficient resolution. Inspect both angles before generation. Game renders are identity references, not the finished portrait.

prompt: Create ONE original FAN ART USER PROFILE PORTRAIT of the {{gender}} {{className}} class from DOFUS, for the Dofus Forge collection. IMAGE 1 is the APPROVED COLLECTION ART STYLE ONLY. IMAGE 2 and IMAGE 3 show the ACTUAL TARGET GAME MODEL from two angles; these define class identity, gender, species, facial features, hairstyle, headwear, original palette and clothing. Never borrow the Iop's orange hair, white eyes, sword, face or pose from the style reference. Keep the target character instantly recognizable from the actual game references. TARGET GAME LOOK: head slot {{headSlot}}, head texture {{headSkin}}, body texture {{bodySkin}}. Preserve this exact face/hairstyle rather than substituting the first head. Use the default outfit while producing the head collection; alternate outfits are a later task. IDENTITY NOTES: {{identityNotes}}. INDIVIDUAL EXPRESSION, POSE AND SMALL STORY: {{individualPose}}. Make an expressive personal fan illustration with its own staging and character, not a gender swap of an existing portrait. Upper torso only, face large near center, readable at 48px. Square avatar that reads inside a centered circular crop; keep headwear and hair contained with top breathing room, shoulders may crop at bottom. Match the approved brush-pen ink and watercolor treatment: lively dark graphite preliminary strokes in a few places, confident tapered black ink with fine and heavy contours, selective hatching, charming asymmetry and expressive French fantasy comic anatomy. Hand-placed loose watercolor fills with small paper gaps near edges, natural varied watercolor boundaries, rich but slightly understated original character colors and a matte finish. Clear main silhouette and economical forms. Clean warm off-white ground with one restrained loose {{watercolorWash}} watercolor wash. No brown paper tint, artificial grunge overlay, generic polished fantasy rendering, plastic, 3D, photorealism, airbrushed gradients, cinematic glow, rim lights, embers, gloss or perfect vector cut-paper shapes. One character and only its small relevant class prop. Opaque square image with watercolor background. No caption, signature, fake notes, lettering, watermark, logo, frame, collage or multiple views.
continuityRules: Preserve the recognizable Dofus class and gender design; the new drawing adds gesture and personality.
Write separate prompts and poses for male and female portraits. Do not reuse a pose merely by changing the hair.
Check existing poses in manifest.json before choosing the new character's expression and story.
Use real target game references, especially for animal faces, masks, headgear and class-specific eyes.
Keep one cohesive ink-and-watercolor collection while allowing individual shapes, expressions, props and quiet wash colors.
Inspect the final drawing both as a square and in a small circular profile crop.
Append each exact final prompt, references and output identity to the collection manifest. Retain older approved entries when creating a new revision.

exports.background: Opaque warm off-white paper and subtle watercolor wash; do not remove unless explicitly requested
exports.profileDisplay: CSS circular crop; retain the complete square master

addingAClass: Add the class's official data and localized name through the project's normal game-data pipeline.
Render the actual male and female models from two angles and inspect their defining traits.
Choose two original poses and expressions, using the existing manifest to avoid repetition.
Generate one image per gender with the approved collection style reference and the target game's model references.
Keep the PNG masters, export the optimized WebP files, append both exact prompts and output metadata to manifest.json, and update collection-preview.webp.

Add both exact public paths to public.profile_avatar_catalog through a new SQL migration and mirror those catalog inserts in supabase/schema.sql. API clients cannot add catalog entries. Apply the migration before releasing the new portraits.

Run the class-avatar, Account page, locale and database checks. The picker follows CLASS_DATA automatically; ensure the new class ships both actual image files and that its paths match the database allowlist.
addingAHead: Refresh game-looks.json from the installed client with python scripts/extract-avatar-looks.py --export-head <slot>. Keep availableAtCreation source order and ids.
Prioritize faces/hairstyles with the default outfit; keep alternate outfits mapped for after all head work.
Render and inspect the selected male and female head from two angles. Do not assume that the second head shares the first head's hood, mask or hairstyle.
Choose a separate pose and expression per portrait after checking earlier poses in manifest.json. Preserve the approved ink-and-watercolor medium.
Save PNG masters and 512px WebP files using <class>-look-<slot>-<m|f> names; keep the original first-head paths unchanged.
Append exact prompts, poses, references, hashes and gameLook head/body slot, id and skin metadata to manifest.json. Retain old approved records.
Run node scripts/sync-avatar-progress.mjs to check completed portraits and regenerate the remaining-head and later-outfit checklists.
Add only completed heads to the picker and exact server catalog paths through a new additive SQL migration mirrored in schema.sql. Apply hosted SQL before deploying the expanded gallery.
